req.title: List returns empty array when db empty
req.statement: The system shall return an empty JSON array on GET /tasks/ when no tasks exist.
triggers: list returns empty array when db empty

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-033 requires GET /tasks/ to return an empty JSON array when no tasks exist. The database contract states 20 rows are pre-loaded before every test, so to test the empty-table scenario we must delete all 20 rows via the API first. We need: (1) a positive test confirming the empty-array response after deleting all rows, (2) a negative test confirming a client error (422) when an invalid query parameter is supplied, and (3) a boundary test confirming the response is exactly [] (zero items) vs. non-empty. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (200, 204, 422), exact response body ([] not just list), exact Content-Type, and exact length (0). We also test the boundary between 0 items and 1 item to catch off-by-one mutations.

tests.name: test_list_tasks_empty_after_deleting_all_rows
actions: Delete all 20 pre-loaded tasks via DELETE /tasks/{id} for ids 1-20
Send GET /tasks/ with no query parameters
expected: Response body is exactly the JSON empty array []
trace: R-TASK-033: system shall return empty JSON array on GET /tasks/ when no tasks exist
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_list_tasks_empty_after_deleting_all_rows():
    client = TestClient(app)
    for task_id in range(1, 21):
        del_resp = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
        assert del_resp.status_code == 204
    response = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body == []
    assert len(body) == 0
    assert "application/json" in response.headers["content-type"]

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_list_tasks_invalid_query_param_returns_422():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/tasks/?skip=-1")
    assert response.status_code == 422
    body = response.json()
    assert "detail" in body
    assert isinstance(body["detail"], list)
    assert len(body["detail"]) >= 1

Assert the single item matches the created task's id and title
expected: After creating one task: HTTP 200 with body of length exactly 1

tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_list_tasks_boundary_zero_vs_one_item():
    client = TestClient(app)
    for task_id in range(1, 21):
        del_resp = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
        assert del_resp.status_code == 204
    empty_resp = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert empty_resp.status_code == 200
    empty_body = empty_resp.json()
    assert empty_body == []
    assert len(empty_body) == 0
    create_resp = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Boundary Task", "completed": False})
    assert create_resp.status_code == 201
    created_id = create_resp.json()["id"]
    assert created_id == 21
    one_resp = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert one_resp.status_code == 200
    one_body = one_resp.json()
    assert len(one_body) == 1
    assert one_body[0]["id"] == created_id
    assert one_body[0]["title"] == "Boundary Task"
    assert one_body[0]["completed"] == False

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_list_tasks_empty_limit_boundary_at_one():
    client = TestClient(app)
    for task_id in range(1, 21):
        del_resp = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
        assert del_resp.status_code == 204
    resp_limit1 = client.get("/tasks/?limit=1")
    assert resp_limit1.status_code == 200
    body_limit1 = resp_limit1.json()
    assert body_limit1 == []
    assert len(body_limit1) == 0
    resp_limit0 = client.get("/tasks/?limit=0")
    assert resp_limit0.status_code == 422
    detail = resp_limit0.json()
    assert "detail" in detail
